stem:
Solve the following simultaneous equations.

\(5x - 3y = 8\); \(3x + y = 2\)
solution:
Method I :

\(5x - 3y = 8\) . . . (I)

\(3x + y = 2\) . . . (II)

Multiplying both sides of equation (II) by 3.

\(9x + 3y = 6\) . . . (III)

Now let us add equations (I) and (III)

\(5x - 3y = 8\)

\(9x + 3y = 6\)

\(14x = 14\)

\(\therefore x = 1\)

Substituting \(x = 1\) in equation (II)

\(3x + y = 2\)

\(\therefore 3 \times 1 + y = 2\)

\(\therefore 3 + y = 2\)

\(\therefore y = -1\)

Solution is \(x = 1\), \(y = -1\); it is also written as \((x, y) = (1, -1)\)

Method II :

\(5x - 3y = 8\) . . . (I)

\(3x + y = 2\) . . . (II)

Let us write value of \(y\) in terms of \(x\) from equation (II) as

\(y = 2 - 3x\) . . . (III)

Substituting this value of \(y\) in equation (I).

\(5x - 3y = 8\)

\(\therefore 5x - 3(2 - 3x) = 8\)

\(\therefore 5x - 6 + 9x = 8\)

\(\therefore 14x - 6 = 8\)

\(\therefore 14x = 8 + 6\)

\(\therefore 14x = 14\)

\(\therefore x = 1\)

Substituting \(x = 1\) in equation (III).

\(y = 2 - 3x\)

\(\therefore y = 2 - 3 \times 1\)

\(\therefore y = 2 - 3\)

\(\therefore y = -1\)

\(x = 1\), \(y = -1\) is the solution.

note: The book prints this worked example as a fill-in-the-boxes activity ('Let's solve the equations by eliminating y. Fill suitably the boxes below.') — every intermediate value is an empty box, though it does print x = 5 in one step. The solution below completes those boxes so the row ships a whole worked solution rather than holes; the method and every printed value are the book's.
solution:
\(3x + 2y = 29\) . . . (I) and \(5x - y = 18\) . . . (II)

Let's solve the equations by eliminating \(y\).

Multiplying equation (II) by 2.

\(\therefore 5x \times 2 - y \times 2 = 18 \times 2\)

\(\therefore 10x - 2y = 36\) . . . (III)

Let's add equations (I) and (III)

\(3x + 2y = 29\)

\(10x - 2y = 36\)

\(13x = 65\)

\(\therefore x = 5\)

Substituting \(x = 5\) in equation (I)

\(3x + 2y = 29\)

\(\therefore 3 \times 5 + 2y = 29\)

\(\therefore 15 + 2y = 29\)

\(\therefore 2y = 29 - 15\)

\(\therefore 2y = 14\)

\(\therefore y = 7\)

\((x, y) = (5, 7)\) is the solution.

note: The book's printed solution says 'Now let's add equations (III) and (V)' — there is no equation (V); the equation being added is (IV). A misprint that does not change the result.
solution:
[Textbook note: the book's printed solution reads 'Now let's add equations (III) and (V)'. There is no equation (V) — the equation added is (IV). The working and the answer are unaffected.]

\(15x + 17y = 21\) . . . (I)

\(17x + 15y = 11\) . . . (II)

In the two equations above, the coefficients of \(x\) and \(y\) are interchanged. While solving such equations we get two simple equations by adding and subtracting the given equations. After solving these equations, we can easily find the solution.

Let's add the two given equations.

\(15x + 17y = 21\)

\(17x + 15y = 11\)

\(32x + 32y = 32\)

Dividing both sides of the equation by 32.

\(x + y = 1\) . . . (III)

Now, let's subtract equation (II) from (I)

\(15x + 17y = 21\)

\(17x + 15y = 11\)

\(-2x + 2y = 10\)

dividing the equation by 2.

\(-x + y = 5\) . . . (IV)

Now let's add equations (III) and (IV).

\(x + y = 1\)

\(-x + y = 5\)

\(\therefore 2y = 6\) \(\therefore y = 3\)

Place this value in equation (III).

\(x + y = 1\)

\(\therefore x + 3 = 1\)

\(\therefore x = 1 - 3\) \(\therefore x = -2\)

\((x, y) = (-2, 3)\) is the solution.

stem:
Solve the following simultaneous equations using Cramer's Rule.

\(5x + 3y = -11\) ; \(2x + 4y = -10\)
solution:
Given equations

\(5x + 3y = -11\)

\(2x + 4y = -10\)

\(\mathrm{D} = \begin{vmatrix} 5 & 3 \\ 2 & 4 \end{vmatrix} = (5 \times 4) - (2 \times 3) = 20 - 6 = 14\)

\(\mathrm{D}_x = \begin{vmatrix} -11 & 3 \\ -10 & 4 \end{vmatrix} = (-11) \times 4 - (-10) \times 3 = -44 - (-30) = -44 + 30 = -14\)

\(\mathrm{D}_y = \begin{vmatrix} 5 & -11 \\ 2 & -10 \end{vmatrix} = 5 \times (-10) - 2 \times (-11) = -50 - (-22) = -50 + 22 = -28\)

\(x = \dfrac{\mathrm{D}_x}{\mathrm{D}} = \dfrac{-14}{14} = -1\) and \(y = \dfrac{\mathrm{D}_y}{\mathrm{D}} = \dfrac{-28}{14} = -2\)

\(\therefore (x, y) = (-1, -2)\) is the solution.

solution:
\(\dfrac{4}{x} + \dfrac{5}{y} = 7\); \(\dfrac{3}{x} + \dfrac{4}{y} = 5\)

\(4\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right) + 5\left(\dfrac{1}{y}\right) = 7\) . . . (I)

\(3\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right) + 4\left(\dfrac{1}{y}\right) = 5\) . . . (II)

Replacing \(\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)\) by \(m\) and \(\left(\dfrac{1}{y}\right)\) by \(n\) in equations (I) and (II), we get

\(4m + 5n = 7\) . . . (III)

\(3m + 4n = 5\) . . . (IV)

On solving these equations we get

\(m = 3\), \(n = -1\)

Now, \(m = \dfrac{1}{x}\) \(\therefore 3 = \dfrac{1}{x}\) \(\therefore x = \dfrac{1}{3}\)

\(n = \dfrac{1}{y}\) \(\therefore -1 = \dfrac{1}{y}\) \(\therefore y = -1\)

\(\therefore\) Solution of given simultaneous equations is \((x, y) = \left(\dfrac{1}{3},\ -1\right)\)

\(\dfrac{4}{x - y} + \dfrac{1}{x + y} = 3\) ; \(\dfrac{2}{x - y} - \dfrac{3}{x + y} = 5\)

\(4\left(\dfrac{1}{x - y}\right) + 1\left(\dfrac{1}{x + y}\right) = 3\) . . . (I)

\(2\left(\dfrac{1}{x - y}\right) - 3\left(\dfrac{1}{x + y}\right) = 5\) . . . (II)

Replacing \(\left(\dfrac{1}{x - y}\right)\) by \(a\) and \(\left(\dfrac{1}{x + y}\right)\) by \(b\) we get

\(4a + b = 3\) . . . (III)

\(2a - 3b = 5\) . . . (IV)

On solving these equations we get, \(a = 1\), \(b = -1\)

But \(a = \left(\dfrac{1}{x - y}\right)\), \(b = \left(\dfrac{1}{x + y}\right)\)

\(\therefore \left(\dfrac{1}{x - y}\right) = 1\), \(\left(\dfrac{1}{x + y}\right) = -1\)

\(\therefore x - y = 1\) . . . (V)

\(x + y = -1\) . . . (VI)

Solving equation (V) and (VI) we get \(x = 0\), \(y = -1\)

\(\therefore\) Solution of the given equations is \((x, y) = (0, -1)\)

stem: The perimeter of a rectangle is 40 cm. The length of the rectangle is more than double its breadth by 2. Find length and breadth.
solution:
Let length of rectangle be \(x\) cm and breadth be \(y\) cm.

From first condition -

\(2(x + y) = 40\)

\(x + y = 20\) . . . (I)

From 2nd condition -

\(x = 2y + 2\)

\(\therefore x - 2y = 2\) . . . (II)

Let's solve eq. (I), (II) by determinant method

\(x + y = 20\)

\(x - 2y = 2\)

\(\mathrm{D} = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -2 \end{vmatrix} = [1 \times (-2)] - (1 \times 1) = -2 - 1 = -3\)

\(\mathrm{D}_x = \begin{vmatrix} 20 & 1 \\ 2 & -2 \end{vmatrix} = [20 \times (-2)] - (1 \times 2) = -40 - 2 = -42\)

\(\mathrm{D}_y = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 20 \\ 1 & 2 \end{vmatrix} = (1 \times 2) - (20 \times 1) = 2 - 20 = -18\)

\(x = \dfrac{\mathrm{D}_x}{\mathrm{D}}\) and \(y = \dfrac{\mathrm{D}_y}{\mathrm{D}}\)

\(\therefore x = \dfrac{-42}{-3}\) and \(y = \dfrac{-18}{-3}\)

\(\therefore x = 14\), \(y = 6\)

\(\therefore\) Length of the rectangle is 14 cm and breadth is 6 cm.

stem:
Sale ! Sale !! Sale !!! only for 2 days

I have some analogue wrist watches and some digital wrist watches. I am going to sell them at a discount.

Sale of 1st day : Analogue watch = 11, Digital watch = 6, Received amount = ₹ 4330

Sale of the 2nd day : Analogue watch = 22, Digital watch = 5, Received amount = ₹ 7330

Find selling price of wrist watch of each type.
solution:
Let selling price of each analogue watch be ₹ \(x\)

Selling price of each digital watch be ₹ \(y\)

From first condition -

\(11x + 6y = 4330\) . . . (I)

from 2nd condition -

\(22x + 5y = 7330\) . . . (II)

multiplying equation (I) by 2 we get,

\(22x + 12y = 8660\) . . . (III)

subtract equation (III) from equation (II).

\(22x + 5y = 7330\) . . . (II)

\(22x + 12y = 8660\) . . . (III)

\(-7y = -1330\)

\(\therefore y = 190\)

Substitute this value of \(y\) in equation (I)

\(11x + 6y = 4330\)

\(\therefore 11x + 6(190) = 4330\)

\(\therefore 11x + 1140 = 4330\)

\(\therefore 11x = 3190\)

\(\therefore x = 290\)

\(\therefore\) selling price of each analogue watch is ₹ 290 and of each digital watch is ₹ 190.

stem: A boat travels 16 km upstream and 24 km downstream in 6 hours. The same boat travels 36 km upstream and 48 km downstream in 13 hours. Find the speed of water current and speed of boat in still water.
solution:
Let the speed of the boat in still water be \(x\) km/hr and the speed of water current be \(y\) km/hr

\(\therefore\) speed of boat in downstream = \((x + y)\) km/hr.

and that in upstream = \((x - y)\) km/hr.

Now distance = speed \(\times\) time \(\therefore\) time = \(\dfrac{\text{distance}}{\text{speed}}\)

Time taken by the boat to travel 16 km upstream = \(\dfrac{16}{x - y}\) hours and it takes \(\dfrac{24}{x + y}\) hours to travel 24 km downstream.

from first condition -

\(\dfrac{16}{x - y} + \dfrac{24}{x + y} = 6\) . . . (I)

from 2nd condition

\(\dfrac{36}{x - y} + \dfrac{48}{x + y} = 13\) . . . (II)

By replacing \(\dfrac{1}{x - y}\) by \(m\) and \(\dfrac{1}{x + y}\) by \(n\) we get

\(16m + 24n = 6\) . . . (III)

\(36m + 48n = 13\) . . . (IV)

Solving equations (III) and (IV) \(m = \dfrac{1}{4}\), \(n = \dfrac{1}{12}\)

Replacing \(m\), \(n\) by their original values we get

\(x - y = 4\) . . . (V)   \(x + y = 12\) . . . (VI)

Solving equations (V), (VI) we get \(x = 8\), \(y = 4\)

\(\therefore\) speed of the boat in still water is 8 km/hr. and speed of water current is 4 km/hr.

stem: A certain amount is equally distributed among certain number of students. Each would get ₹ 2 less if 10 students were more and each would get ₹ 6 more if 15 students were less. Find the number of students and the amount distributed.
solution:
Let the number of students be \(x\) and amount given to each student be ₹ \(y\).

\(\therefore\) Total amount distributed is \(xy\)

From the first condition we get,

\((x + 10)(y - 2) = xy\)

\(\therefore xy - 2x + 10y - 20 = xy\)

\(\therefore -2x + 10y = 20\)

\(\therefore -x + 5y = 10\) . . . (I)

From the 2nd condition we get,

\((x - 15)(y + 6) = xy\)

\(\therefore xy + 6x - 15y - 90 = xy\)

\(\therefore 6x - 15y = 90\)

\(\therefore 2x - 5y = 30\) . . . (II)

Adding equations (I) and (II)

\(-x + 5y = 10\)

\(2x - 5y = 30\)

\(x = 40\)

Substitute this value of \(x\) in equation (I)

\(-x + 5y = 10\)

\(\therefore -40 + 5y = 10\)

\(\therefore 5y = 50\)

\(\therefore y = 10\)

Total amount distributed is \(= xy = 40 \times 10 =\) ₹ 400.

\(\therefore\) ₹ 400 distributed equally among 40 students.

stem: A three digit number is equal to 17 times the sum of its digits; If the digits are reversed, the new number is 198 more than the old number ; also the sum of extreme digits is less than the middle digit by unity. Find the original number.
solution:
Let the digit in hundreds place be \(x\) and that in unit place be \(y\).

| H | T | unit |
|---|---|---|
| \(x\) | \(x + y + 1\) | \(y\) |

\(\therefore\) the three digit number is \(100x + 10(x + y + 1) + y\)

\(= 100x + 10x + 10y + 10 + y = 110x + 11y + 10\)

the sum of the digits in the given number \(= x + (x + y + 1) + y = 2x + 2y + 1\)

\(\therefore\) From first condition

Given number \(= 17 \times\) (sum of the digits)

\(\therefore 110x + 11y + 10 = 17 \times (2x + 2y + 1)\)

\(\therefore 110x + 11y + 10 = 34x + 34y + 17\)

\(\therefore 76x - 23y = 7\) . . . (I)

The number obtained by reversing the digits

\(= 100y + 10(x + y + 1) + x = 110y + 11x + 10\)

Given number \(= 110x + 11y + 10\)

From 2nd condition, Given number \(+\ 198 =\) new number.

\(110x + 11y + 10 + 198 = 110y + 11x + 10\)

\(99x - 99y = -198\)

\(x - y = -2\)

\(\therefore x = y - 2\) . . . (II)

Substitute this value of \(x\) in equation (I).

\(\therefore 76(y - 2) - 23y = 7\)

\(\therefore 76y - 152 - 23y = 7\)

\(53y = 159\)

\(\therefore y = 3\) \(\therefore\) the digit in units place is \(= 3\)

Substitute this value in equation (II)

\(x = y - 2\)

\(\therefore x = 3 - 2 = 1\)

\(\therefore x = 1\) \(\therefore\) The digit in hundred's place is 1

the digit in ten's place is \(3 + 1 + 1 = 5\)

\(\therefore\) the number is 153.
